title: Introduce local shellplay RAG runner with contracted tool stubs and telemetry presets
author: Sofia Rossi
commits: Initial scaffold: add runner, README, and sample tool stubs
Add telemetry presets + otel config and instructions
Polish CLI flags, add streaming checkbox and retry logic
Docs: usage examples and troubleshooting notes
Fix linting and CI unit-test flakiness (telemetry mock)
release_notes: New lightweight local RAG runner quickstart (rag-shellplay) that demonstrates a minimal tool-calling contract, local CLI workflow, and telemetry presets for easy onboarding.
description:
Summary: Adds a compact, runnable quickstart called 'rag-shellplay' that demonstrates a local RAG authoring + execution loop focused on developer debugging and contract-first tool stubs. Motivation: teams often need a tiny reproducible runner to iterate on prompt/tool contracts, structured outputs, and telemetry without spinning up full infra. This quickstart provides a CLI-driven loop, a typed tool stub pattern, streaming toggles, and out-of-the-box OpenTelemetry presets to show end-to-end traces and token-level timing.

What this change includes: - A runnable Python runner (runner.py) that executes a short RAG flow: query -> retrieval mock -> prompt -> model call (OpenAI-compatible shim) -> tool invocation (contracted stub) -> structured output validation. The runner supports --stream, --dry-run, and --replay flags. - A sample tool stub (tool_stubs/sample_tool.py) that demonstrates an idempotent contract: input schema, output schema, and error shape; includes typed examples and simple local state simulated with an in-memory store. - README with step-by-step quickstart, common prompts, and troubleshooting tips for local indexing vs. remote index. - OpenTelemetry presets (telemetry/otel-presets.yaml) and docs showing how to pipe traces into common backends (Jaeger/Zipkin) and how to enable token timing. - Minimal smoke CI workflow (ci/quickstart-smoke/runner-smoke.yml) that runs the quickstart in a sandboxed container and asserts smoke outputs and telemetry headers.

Checklist (completed): [x] Quickstart runner scaffolded and documented [x] Tool stub contract example included [x] Telemetry presets + docs added [x] Smoke CI added and green [x] Reviewed and approved by reviewers 

Commits: See commits list above for progressive changes.

Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/rag-shellplay/README.md: usage, examples, FAQ, prompts gallery - quickstarts/rag-shellplay/runner.py: main CLI runner, streaming wrapper, retry/backoff, mock retrieval - quickstarts/rag-shellplay/tool_stubs/sample_tool.py: typed contract, unit tests, helpful assert helpers - quickstarts/rag-shellplay/telemetry/otel-presets.yaml: example OTEL config and env var notes - docs/reference/rag-shellplay.md: cross-linked docsite page with expanded debugging advice - ci/quickstart-smoke/runner-smoke.yml: lightweight CI smoke harness (runs in 60s)

Review conversation (high-level): - Evan Park (reviewer): Asked for clearer boundaries between 'tool contract' and 'app-specific handler' and requested that the tool stub expose a validate_schema function. Response: updated sample_tool.py to include validate_schema and added unit tests. - Priya Nair: Requested an example of failure-mode instrumentation (how to spot retry storms). Response: added a small section in README and a telemetry example that annotates retries and backoff durations in spans. - Diego Martinez: Noted streaming behavior should be opt-in and asked for deterministic replay; added --replay flag that records token deltas to a local file for deterministic replays.

CI and testing: The PR added a smoke job to ci/quickstart-smoke that runs the runner with a mocked model endpoint and asserts structured output and presence of telemetry headers. The main CI run initially failed due to a flaky telemetry mock; fixed in second commit and all checks passed. CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and migration: This is additive; no breaking changes. The quickstart is optional and lives under quickstarts/rag-shellplay. It references the OpenAI-compatible shim already present in the monorepo.

How to try locally (short): 1) python -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate 2) pip install -r quickstarts/rag-shellplay/requirements.txt 3) python quickstarts/rag-shellplay/runner.py --query "what's the latest on accounts receivable" --stream 4) Start Jaeger and run with TELEMETRY_BACKEND=jaeger to see spans.

Notes for docs maintainers: The PR includes docs/reference/rag-shellplay.md but the docsite navigation will be updated in a follow-up PR to avoid a large nav churn in this change.

Known limitations: - Retrieval is mocked to keep the quickstart lightweight; we include a small section showing how to swap in a real indexer. - The sample tool is intentionally minimal; for production usage, recommend wiring to an idempotent external API with retries and circuit-breakers.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-27 after approvals from reviewers.

Related: Linked Linear tickets ENG-1345 (quickstart scaffold) and PM-220 (developer onboarding for RAG).
